pages.title: What went well?
pages.instruction: Read Laura’s feedback before preparing a reply
pages.author: Laura Hughes · client
pages.subject: Tuesday’s presentation · first part
paragraphs: Thank you and your team for the presentation Raj delivered on Tuesday. He really knows the project, and he has a friendly style. The slides had a lot of information. To be fair, there was a lot to say in thirty minutes.

pages.title: What still needs attention?
pages.instruction: Separate the concern from the request for next week
pages.author: Laura Hughes · client
pages.subject: Tuesday’s presentation · next step
paragraphs: Some of us found the second part a bit hard to understand, and we didn’t get an answer to my question about the deadline. It might be worth meeting again next week, just for the important points. Would Thursday at ten work? It would be great if you could be there too.

pages.title: Explain Laura’s message
pages.instruction: Use her words as evidence; distinguish facts from your interpretation

items.prompt: What does Laura value, and what concerns her?
items.hint: She values …, but she points out …
items.answer: She values Raj’s knowledge and style but found the second part hard to follow

items.prompt: What does she want to happen next?
items.answer: Another meeting on Thursday at ten, with Ana there too

pages.title: Ana’s first attempt
pages.instruction: Listen for the criticism and Kim’s reaction

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So, the big talk with Raj is tomorrow?
lines.audioText: So, the big talk with Raj is tomorrow?
lines.translation: Então a grande conversa com o Raj é amanhã?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes. I’ll start with: “You really know the project, and I like your style.”
lines.audioText: Yes. I’ll start with: “You really know the project, and I like your style.”
lines.translation: Sim. Vou começar com: “Você conhece muito bem o projeto, e eu gosto do seu estilo.”

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Then: “You talked too fast and just read the slides.”
lines.audioText: Then: “You talked too fast and just read the slides.”
lines.translation: Depois: “Você falou rápido demais e só leu os slides.”

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Hmm. That sounds a bit harsh
lines.audioText: Hmm. That sounds a bit harsh.

questions.prompt: What does Ana plan to criticise?
questions.answer: Raj spoke too fast and read the slides

pages.title: Make the concern specific
pages.instruction: Follow the change from an accusation to an observation

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Sure, but it might come across as an attack. Try: “It seemed a little rushed.”
lines.audioText: Sure, but it might come across as an attack. Try: “It seemed a little rushed.”
lines.translation: Claro, mas pode soar como um ataque. Tenta: “Pareceu um pouco corrido.”

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: “It seemed a little rushed.” And for the slides, maybe—
lines.audioText: “It seemed a little rushed.” And for the slides, maybe—
lines.translation: “Pareceu um pouco corrido.” E, para os slides, talvez—

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Maybe “The slides tend to—” Sorry, go on
lines.audioText: Maybe “The slides tend to—” Sorry, go on.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: No, that’s it! “The slides tend to have a lot of text. You might want to cut some.”
lines.audioText: No, that’s it! “The slides tend to have a lot of text. You might want to cut some.”
lines.translation: Não, é isso! “Os slides costumam ter muito texto. Talvez valha cortar alguns.”

questions.answer: Describe the effect and make the suggested change specific

pages.title: Agree on a useful next step
pages.instruction: Listen for the proposal and the reason to be fair

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Much better. And the client’s question? That one’s more serious
lines.audioText: Much better. And the client’s question? That one’s more serious.
lines.translation: Muito melhor. E a pergunta da cliente? Essa é mais séria

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: “I wonder if we could prepare the answers together next time.”
lines.audioText: “I wonder if we could prepare the answers together next time.”
lines.translation: “Será que a gente podia preparar as respostas juntos da próxima vez?”

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Perfect. Oh, and start with a question: “How do you think it went?”
lines.audioText: Perfect. Oh, and start with a question: “How do you think it went?”
lines.translation: Perfeito. Ah, e começa com uma pergunta: “Como você acha que foi?”

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Good idea. To be fair, it was his first big client. There’s a learning curve

items.hint: It might come across as …, especially if …

items.prompt: How would you raise the issue?
items.cue: Offer an observation and a constructive suggestion
items.hint: I’ve noticed … I wonder if we could …

pages.title: Separate a pattern from an impression
pages.instruction: Choose wording that matches the evidence you actually have

rows.subject: A pattern
rows.example: The slides tend to have a lot of text.

rows.subject: A view
rows.example: The second half seemed a little rushed.

rows.subject: Possible effect
rows.example: That comment might come across as an attack.

pages.note: Tend to needs evidence of a repeated pattern. This email concerns one presentation; without more evidence, describe an impression rather than a pattern.

pages.title: Invite a response without losing the point
pages.instruction: Keep a suggestion specific and open to discussion

rows.subject: An option
rows.example: You might want to cut some text from the slides.

rows.subject: A shared action
rows.example: I wonder if we could prepare the answers together next time.

pages.note: A softer opening does not replace a clear request. Relationship, authority and urgency affect the wording.

pages.title: Make the feedback useful
pages.instruction: Give Raj specific feedback and agree on one practical next step

pages.title: Raj responds to the feedback
pages.instruction: Listen for what he accepts and the point he wants to clarify
pages.message: Hi, Ana, it’s Raj. Thanks for today. Really. It was… constructive. I’ll take it on board. I guess I did talk a bit fast. But, to be fair, nobody told me Laura would ask about the deadline. I didn’t know how to handle it. And the slides were Sarah’s. I only saw them on Monday. Anyway. I’ll try not to rush next time. Oh, and Thursday? I wonder if I could talk to Laura directly. Just me. I think it’s worth trying. Let me know. Thanks
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana, it’s Raj. Thanks for today. Really. It was… constructive. I’ll take it on board. I guess I did talk a bit fast. But, to be fair, nobody told me Laura would ask about the deadline. I didn’t know how to handle it. And the slides were Sarah’s. I only saw them on Monday. Anyway. I’ll try not to rush next time. Oh, and Thursday? I wonder if I could talk to Laura directly. Just me. I think it’s worth trying. Let me know. Thanks.
pages.greeting: Can we talk about the presentation?

items.prompt: What has Raj accepted, and what does he dispute?
items.cue: Separate agreement from the remaining concern
items.hint: He accepts …, but he points out …
items.answer: He accepts that he rushed; he says he was not told about the deadline question and had only seen Sarah’s slides on Monday

pages.title: Keep the reply constructive
pages.instruction: Acknowledge Raj’s point while keeping Laura’s request clear

items.hint: I can see why … Laura has asked … Could we agree …?
items.answer: Acknowledge his preference, explain that Laura asked Ana to attend, then agree how to share the questions
